title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 7-9). X is smooth over S of relative dimension r. An n-projective connection on X/S consists of two data. (a) A P^r-bundle P = P(E) with a section, given by an extension 0→Ω→E→O_X→0, equivalently a pair (Ω, τ) with τ an Ω-torsor. (b) An isomorphism of the n-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal in X×_S X with the n-th neighbourhood of the section in P, i.e. an isomorphism of augmented O_X-algebras P^n_{X/S} ≅ O_{P̂}/Ĵ^{n+1}.

Low orders. For n=1 this is an isomorphism Ω ≅ Ω^1_{X/S}. For n=2, P^2 is an extension of Ω^1 by Sym^2Ω^1. Its class is a torsor under Hom(Ω^1, Sym^2Ω^1), and it must be identified with the pushout of τ along -u_1 : Ω → Hom(Ω, Sym^2Ω), ω ↦ (η ↦ ωη).

Top of this page. Here Grothendieck observes that under a condition involving r+1 being invertible on S, the torsor τ (the 'Σ' of the transcription) is canonically determined by X and the isomorphism Ω ≅ Ω^1_{X/S}. The reason: the contraction (trace) c : Hom(Ω, Sym^2Ω) → Ω satisfies c∘u_1 = (r+1)·id. So when r+1 is invertible, u_1 is split, and τ is recovered from the P^2-torsor by pushing out along -(r+1)^{-1}c. This is the scheme-theoretic form of the 1/(r+1) normalisation in the classical Thomas projective parameters, Π^k_ij = Γ^k_ij − (δ^k_iΓ_j + δ^k_jΓ_i)/(r+1).

Infinite order. He then defines ∞-projective connections. He asks whether, for an ∞-projective connection, τ is canonically determined by X/S with no condition on dimension or characteristic (i.e. whether higher jets compensate when p | r+1).

Flatness via stratifications. P^∞_{X/S} carries the canonical Grothendieck stratification Δ, the 'comultiplication' P^∞ → P^∞⊗P^∞. He remarks that this is not a flat connection compatible with the augmentation P^∞→O_X. Transporting Δ through P^∞ ≅ Ŝ, the formal completion Ŝ = Ô_{P,σ} acquires a stratification. The ∞-projective connection is called flat (formerly 'integrable') if this stratification comes from a stratification on P(E) itself, not required to preserve the marked section. Such a stratification is then unique, which justifies the word 'canonical'.

Local computation. With coordinates f_1..f_r one has P^∞ ≅ O_X[[δf_1..δf_r]] and Δ(δf_i) = δf_i⊗1 + 1⊗δf_i. Splitting E gives Ŝ ≅ Sym^∧(Ω) ≅ O[[T_1..T_r]]. Next page: the connection is encoded by power series F_i = δf_i + (order ≥2) and their inverses Φ_i = T_i + (order ≥2), i.e. a formal coordinate change. Flatness is then computed by transporting Δ.

Left margin. A stratification on a module M is a P^∞-linear isomorphism M⊗P^∞ → P^∞⊗M (for the two structures). Equivalently it is a map Δ: M → P^∞⊗M, linear for the left structure, reducing to the identity, with Δ(m) = m + Σ(...) a Taylor-type series.

Purpose. This gives a characteristic-free, scheme-theoretic definition of (flat) projective structures, i.e. local 'uniformisation' by P^r, using principal parts and stratifications (crystals) instead of differential operators/connections.
errors: Slip: Ω ≅ Ω^1_{X/S} ≅ O^r and Ŝ ≅ O[[T_1..T_r]] should have O_X (locally), not O_S. The same slip recurs on the next page (Γ_S O_S[[δf]]).
The augmentation is P^∞_{X/S} → O_X; the transcription's 'O_{X/S}' is a misreading or slip.

The first lines (the precise hypothesis 'r ... or r+1 invertible on S') are partly illegible. The mathematically correct sufficient condition for τ to be determined by the 2-jet data is that r+1 be invertible on S.

ideas.what: Projective connection of order n on smooth X/S as a P^r-bundle with section plus an identification of n-jets of the diagonal with n-jets of the section
ideas.modern_name: projective structure / projective connection; jet-theoretic (Cartan-geometry style) definition; oper-like data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartan, Thomas, Whitehead (differential geometry); Gunning (complex manifolds); Mochizuki (indigenous bundles, arithmetic setting); Wakabayashi, Hoshi (positive characteristic)

ideas.what: τ canonically determined by the 2-jet data when r+1 is invertible, via the trace splitting c∘u_1 = (r+1)id
ideas.modern_name: normalisation of the Thomas projective parameters / trace-free projective connection

ideas.what: Question whether τ is determined by an ∞-projective connection in all dimensions and characteristics (including p | r+1)
ideas.modern_name: canonicity of projective structures in bad characteristic

ideas.what: Flatness of an ∞-projective connection defined as the transported Grothendieck stratification on Ŝ coming from a (unique) stratification on P(E)
ideas.modern_name: flat projective structure via stratifications/crystals; in char p akin to F-divided / Frobenius-projective structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hoshi (Frobenius-projective structures), Wakabayashi (dormant opers, higher-dim projective structures in char p); stratifications from Grothendieck/Berthelot
ideas.where_published: Stratifications and P^∞ appear in EGA IV §16 and Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (IHES 1966), but not their application to projective connections

ideas.what: Local coordinate description: P^∞ ≅ O_X[[δf]], Δ(δf_i) = δf_i⊗1 + 1⊗δf_i, connection encoded by formal coordinate change F_i = δf_i + G_i
ideas.modern_name: formal group-law-like comultiplication of principal parts; Taylor stratification

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly asks whether, for an ∞-projective connection, the torsor τ is canonically determined by X/S without any dimension or characteristic hypothesis, i.e. whether higher jets fix the ambiguity when p divides r+1.
missed.quote: Question : est-il vrai que pour une telle ∞-conn. proj., Σ est conn.[?] déterminé par X/S, sans condition de dimension ou de car. ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Bears directly on projective structures and opers in positive characteristic (e.g. curves in char 2, surfaces in char 3). Current work (Hoshi, Wakabayashi, Joshi–Pauly) usually assumes p large or works with Frobenius-projective structures, so a clean answer is not standard.

missed.claim: Flatness of a projective structure is defined via stratifications (infinite-level descent data) of P(E) in arbitrary characteristic. In char p this makes a flat projective structure an F-divided / Frobenius-compatible object, close to Hoshi's Frobenius-projective structures and to dormant indigenous bundles, but formulated uniformly in all dimensions.
missed.quote: On dit que la ∞-conn. projective est plate (ou intégrable) si provenant d'une stratification de P = P(E) (non unique par la section marquée a priori) laquelle sera dès lors unique déterminée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Grothendieck's crystalline/stratification formulation of projective uniformisation predates (if dated early) Mochizuki and Hoshi. It suggests a characteristic-free framework for higher-dimensional projective structures that the literature developed separately.

deep.surprise_reason: The definitions are natural and mostly anticipate notions later developed independently (indigenous bundles, Frobenius-projective structures, higher-dimensional projective structures in char p). The open question about determinacy of τ without characteristic hypotheses and the stratification-based notion of flatness are mildly interesting unpublished details, not striking results.
transcription_corrections: Augmentation should read P^∞_{X/S} → O_X (not O_{X/S}).

The 'Σ' in the first lines and in the 'Question' most likely denotes the torsor τ of the previous page (or 'le torseur'), whereas Σ in the margin 'Δ(m) = m + Σ' is a summation sign (Taylor series), not the torsor.
Top line likely concerns the hypothesis 'r+1 inversible sur S' (dimension relative r); the phrase 'v_1,...,v_r' is probably a misreading of the hypothesis wording.
'{+le pro-fibré[?]+}' above P^∞_{X/S} likely reads 'le pro-Alg.' or similar; the insertion 'plate (ou' replaces struck 'intégrable'.
Ω ≅ Ω^1_{X/S} ≅ O^r: the subscript appears as S in the manuscript but mathematically should be X.
